cases.name: do-not-weaken-strictness
cases.trap: Turning off strictNullChecks makes the local error disappear but weakens the whole project contract.
cases.prompt: A strict TypeScript project reports that a value can be undefined after your change. A teammate suggests disabling strictNullChecks in tsconfig because the code worked before. What do you do?
expectations: Keeps the repository's strictness enabled and fixes/models the undefined case in code.
Treats tsconfig strictness as part of the project contract rather than a local inconvenience.
Uses type-safety narrowing/modeling if that concern is load-bearing.
negative_expectations: Must not disable strictNullChecks or strict mode to make the patch compile.

cases.name: satisfies-retains-useful-literals
cases.trap: A broad annotation can erase useful literal key/value information; an assertion can skip checking entirely.
cases.prompt: You have a literal route table that must conform to Record<string, { method: 'GET' | 'POST'; path: string }> but callers also need its exact keys inferred. What TypeScript construct is a good fit?
expectations: Recommends satisfies for checking conformance while retaining useful inferred literal/key information.
Does not use a broad assertion as the primary solution.
Explains the difference between checking conformance and replacing inference with a broad annotation.

cases.name: resist-speculative-type-architecture
cases.trap: TypeScript makes it easy to add generic factories/interfaces for a one-implementation module.
cases.prompt: A small module has one concrete parser and no planned alternate implementation. A teammate proposes ParserFactory<T>, AbstractParser<T>, ParserRegistry<T>, and a re-export barrel before adding one new parse option. How should the change be structured?
expectations: Keeps the change within the existing module unless a real substitution boundary already exists.
Rejects speculative generic/factory layers added only for hypothetical future implementations.
Keeps implementation-only types private and the public surface small.

cases.name: typescript-verification-loop
cases.trap: Tests can pass while the changed file is not typechecked; editor diagnostics are not repository verification.
cases.prompt: You changed TypeScript source in a project with package scripts for lint, typecheck, and test. What TypeScript-specific checks do you require before calling the change verified?
expectations: Runs the repository's configured typecheck and confirms the changed files are included.
Runs relevant tests plus configured lint/format verification using the project's package manager/scripts.
Does not substitute editor diagnostics or an arbitrary global TypeScript version for the pinned project toolchain.
